To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the default values used by SAS for estimating a two-level cross-classified model are suboptimal.

(1) the default values of the 5 information criteria used by SAS PROC Mixed for estimating 2-level cross- classified random effects models are inadequate for selecting the correct model; (2) the modified AICC, CAICC, CAICc, HQICc, and BICc perform much better; and (3) the default values for the χ2 difference test for testing the significance of the difference in fit for 2 nested cross- classified random-effects models perform well, although the

(1) the information criteria performed well in identifying the correct model when the number of level-1 units was used to modify the AICC, BIC, CAIC, and HQIC and the average number of level-2 units was used to modified the AICC and (2) the χ2 diff performed well in identifying a model that did not fit better than another model when the average number of units in a level-2 classification was used to modify AIC, AICC, CAI
In summary, our research is concerned with
a specific class of models, the cross-classified random effect (CCRE) model, and the problem of choosing among a set of models of this type.
the problem of model selection for a cross-classified random effect (CCE) model.
the evaluation of information criteria use for correct cross-classified random effect model selection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AICC, AIC, BIC and CAIC are all good choices, with the AICC being the best.
the information criteria should be used with caution, and that researchers should not blindly use the default values provided in software packages.
the default values of the 5 indices are too large for most applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the default values for the information criteria are not the best choice for model selection in the case of cross-classified random effect models.
the default values for the AICC and CAIC should be modified to N + m and that the default value for the HQIC should be N, and that the default BIC should be modified by a constant.
the default values for the information criteria used by SAS PROC mixed should not be used for model selection in cross-classified random effect models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the default values for information criteria in the SAS PROC MIXED output for cross-classified random effect models may not be optimal.
the default values of the information criteria for the cross-classified random effect model in PROC MIXED are not optimal.
the default sample sizes used in SAS PROC MIXED are inadequate for cross-classified random models, especially those with a small number of level 2 units (m) or a small number of nonempty cells (c).
